newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Metorex consortium wins ZCCM copper project.
newsitem.headline: Metorex consortium wins ZCCM copper project.

text.p: South Africa's Maranda Mines Ltd said on Friday that the Metorex consortium, in which it holds a 30 percent stake, had been awarded Zambian Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd Chibuluma copper project.

It said the consortium would acquire an 85 percent shareholding in the Chibuluma project for an unspecified cash payment on September 30, further cobalt contribution linked payments and a financial commitment to commence development development of the project.
The financing of the purchase price and capital expenditure was currently under review and an announcement in this regard would be made shortly, it said.
The Chibuluma project comprises an existing operating mine, Chibuluma West, currently producting some 9,500 tonnes of copper metal and 200 tonnes of cobalt a year.

The mine is one of the lower cost producers within ZCCM and has a proven reserve of a minimum of three years with the geological potential to continue operations beyond that, Maranda said in a statement.
It operates at a scale of some 35,000 tonnes a month, while the ore is treated at the Nkana concentrator where a final cathode copper is produced on contract basis.

The second component of the project, known as Chibuluma South, is a drill proven ore reserve grading 4.25 percent copper with a life of some 14 years at a scale of 40,000 tonnes a month to produce 15,000 tonnes of copper metal a year.
Development at the Chibuluma South project is envisaged on completion of engineering studies as soon as possible to phase its with the closure of Chibuluma West.

The Metorex consortium, is jointly held by Maranda, Canadian development company Crew Development Corp, which holds 35 percent, South African investment bank Genbel Securities Ltd with 20 percent and unlisted junior mining company Metorex Ltd with 15 percent.
